assumptions: Only three intent types are supported (connect_pins, connect_pin_to_net, ensure_pullup), so component additions/replacements (USB-C receptacle for J1, AMS1117-3.3 LDO U3, CP2102N U4, decoupling caps, 0R strap R6, test point TP1) cannot be expressed here and are left to the component/layout stages.
I2C bus nets are named SDA and SCL; U1 GPIO21 = SDA, U1 GPIO22 = SCL per IF-001.
4.7k pull-ups on SDA and SCL to +3V3 per IF-002; 100 kHz standard mode with <400 pF bus capacitance (IF-003) is satisfied with two devices.
U2 VCC (pin 1) is currently on no net; it is added to +3V3, and U2 GND (pin 2) is added to GND to close PWR-003/PWR-008 and TEST-004.

U2 pin 5 (ADD0) is already on GND in the baseline netlist; the intent restates it as an intentional strap for address 0x48 (IF-004). Physically it should be a 0R 0603 jumper (R6), which cannot be expressed as an intent.

U1 EN (pin 8) is moved off the +3V3 net onto a dedicated EN net with a 10k pull-up to +3V3 (IF-007). The 100 nF from EN to GND cannot be expressed with the supported intents and must be added as component C5.
U1 GPIO25 (pin 5) is terminated to a dedicated GPIO25_TP net feeding test point TP1 (IF-008) rather than a no-connect flag, matching the component stage decision.

PWR_FLAG symbols: #FLG01 is assigned to VBUS and #FLG02 to +3V3; a third flag is required on GND for PWR-007 but no third PWR_FLAG symbol exists in the pin table, so the GND flag must be added as a new symbol (cannot be expressed as an intent).
#PWR01 (+3V3) and #PWR02 (GND) power symbols are tied to their respective rails to make the global rails explicit.

USB_D+/USB_D- baseline connections (J1.3->U1.6, J1.2->U1.7) are left unchanged as intents; note that ESP32-WROOM-32 has no USB PHY, so per the component stage these pins are really UART TXD0/RXD0 and the D+/D- pair should terminate on the CP2102N bridge (U4). This re-mapping requires new symbols and is flagged rather than proposed as an intent.
VBUS_FILT, the LDO input/output connections, and the 5.1k CC1/CC2 pull-downs (IF-006) require the new USB-C receptacle and LDO symbols and therefore cannot be proposed as intents at this stage.
The 90 Ohm differential pair spec (IF-005) is treated as best-effort symmetric routing since COST-003 forbids controlled impedance; acceptable for USB full speed.

intents.purpose: PWR-003/TEST-004: drive TMP102 VCC from the 3.3 V logic rail; power_in pin is currently unconnected.
PWR-008/TEST-004: tie TMP102 GND into the single common ground net (currently missing from GND).
IF-001: I2C data from ESP32 GPIO21 to TMP102 SDA at 3.3 V logic.
IF-001: I2C clock from ESP32 GPIO22 to TMP102 SCL at 100 kHz standard mode.
IF-002/IF-003: open-drain SDA idle-high bias, 0.70 mA sink, rise time within 100 kHz standard mode.
IF-002/IF-003: open-drain SCL idle-high bias, 0.70 mA sink, rise time within 100 kHz standard mode.
IF-004: ADD0 strapped low to select I2C address 0x48 and never left floating (intentional strap, to be implemented as 0R jumper R6).
IF-007: move ESP32 EN off the +3V3 net onto a dedicated RC-strapped enable node.
IF-007: 10k pull-up forming the EN power-on delay with the 100 nF to GND (C5), so EN is released after the 3.3 V rail settles.
IF-008/TEST-001: terminate spare GPIO25 on a defined net routed to test point TP1 so no pin is left unconnected in ERC.
PWR-007/TEST-004: PWR_FLAG marks VBUS as driven since the USB receptacle pin is passive.
PWR-007/TEST-004: PWR_FLAG marks the +3V3 rail as driven for the U1.1 and U2.1 power_in pins.
Make the global +3V3 rail symbol explicit on the regulated logic rail (PWR-003).
Make the global GND rail symbol explicit on the single common ground net (PWR-008).
PWR-001: 5 V VBUS input from the USB receptacle feeds the bulk decoupling and LDO input.
PWR-008: USB cable ground return joins the single common GND net.
IF-005: retain the D+ leg of the USB 2.0 full-speed pair (best-effort symmetric routing; see assumption on the required USB-UART bridge).
IF-005: retain the D- leg of the USB 2.0 full-speed pair (best-effort symmetric routing; see assumption on the required USB-UART bridge).
